ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture, the solid-line road goes from M through K and L to N, and is a horizontal straight line. Below the segment from K to L, a dashed detour route is drawn: from K vertically downward, then horizontally to the right, and finally vertically upward back to L. The left side marks the vertical descent distance as 3 km; the bottom edge of the dashed route is parallel to KL, and the two ends are respectively directly below K and L. Reasoning: the original route in the repair segment goes directly along KL; the detour route in this segment goes 3 km downward + a horizontal dashed segment of equal length to KL + 3 km upward. The horizontal part equal in length to KL cancels with the original KL, so the extra distance traveled comes only from the two vertical segments: 3 + 3 = 6 km.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a straight solid road M-K-L-N, with only segment KL replaced by a dashed rectangular detour: go down from K, across horizontally, then up to L. The vertical drop is labeled 3 km, and the dashed bottom horizontal segment is parallel to KL, so it has the same length as KL. Compare only the repaired segment: direct route uses KL, detour uses 3 km down + KL across + 3 km up. The KL portions cancel, leaving 3+3=6 km extra.
